subject: comparison of random walk precision parameter between two models

messages.author: 26579d78ee0800d6
messages.subject: comparison of random walk precision parameter between two models
parts:
Dear INLA users,

I am modelling population trends for different species using random walks, following the example set in Zuur's book. 

I'm wondering if it makes sense to compare the precision parameter of the random walks between species as an indication of their variability, i.e. if we can expect certain species to change more abruptly between years than others. My main concern is that abundances are very different between species, and I'm not completely sure how that affects the comparability of the precision parameter. 

In case more detail is needed, I model each species independently and my models look something like this:
 
comp <- ~ Intercept_p(1) + rw_species1(year, model = "rw2")

lik_p <- like(pa_df$biomass_species1~ Intercept_p +  rw_species1,
              data = pa_df,
              family = "gamma")

joint_m <- bru(comp,   lik_p)

I do the same for each species.


What do you think?  Hope this question is not too out of place.

Thanks,

Paula

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] comparison of random walk precision parameter between two models
parts:
you can do that, but add argument scale.model=TRUE to the rw_species1

this will scale the marginal variance of the RW so that precision=1 means
variance=1.

otherwise, the comparison will depend on if the number of years are different;
see the vignette (in INLA) about 'scaling'
